newsitem.title: CANADA: Consortium plans C$1.4-bln LNG plant in Canada.
newsitem.headline: Consortium plans C$1.4-bln LNG plant in Canada.

text.p: A consortium of Canadian, U.S. and South Korean companies has announced plans for a C$1.4 billion liquefied natural gas plant to be located on the northwest coast of British Columbia.

Construction of the PAC-RIM LNG Inc project, which still required a number of regulatory approvals, was scheduled to start in the summer of 1997 with first production planned for the end of 1999, the consortium said.
PAC-RIM said in a statement that it signed an interim agreement to supply 3.5 million tonnes per year of LNG to South Korean state-owned Korean Gas Corp when output started.

The consortium said the plant would be located at Bish Creek, located on Haisla Indian Nation lands belonging to the Kitamaat Village Council, 12 kilometers from Kitimat, British Columbia. Negotiations were proceeding between PAC-RIM and the Kitamaat Village Council for the use of the lands, the group said.

The consortium includes Capital Projects Group Inc and BAS Ventures Inc, both of Calgary, Phillips Petroleum of Bartlesville, Oklahoma, Bechtel Enterprises Inc of San Francisco, Daewoo Corp of Seoul, South Korea and Korea Gas Corp.

PAC-RIM said the interim deal to supply LNG to Korea Gas Corp was expected to lead to a sales and purchase agreement. The agreement would confirm LNG price, quantity, delivery schedule, production buildup and technical specifications.
It said the agreement was expected in February 1997.
PAC-RIM vice-president Wilfred Blood said in an interview that the plant would take in about 500 million cubic feet per day of natural gas from British Columbia and Alberta.
"We've had discussions with gas producers and we're about to go into further discussions with them that hopefully will culminate in gas supply contracts," Blood said.
"We have commitments in writing subject to satisfactory price negotiations," Blood said. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
